description:
Hi! I'm a Software Engineer from Barbados, I have experience with Python, APIs, databases, and web development.

Our project, EarthScope, aims to explore environmental trends using NASA data.

I'm looking for teammates interested in data science, Earth science, statistics, UI/UX, or data visualization. All experience levels are welcome! Let's collaborate and build something meaningful.
summary:
Ocean Observatory is an interactive Earth science application developed by Team Bajan Chief for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Designed to address the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, EarthScope uses NASA POWER environmental data to investigate long-term temperature and humidity trends, with a particular focus on the Caribbean.

Users can select locations, explore historical measurements, compare environmental trends, and assess statistical significance through interactive visualizations. The application uses linear regression, confidence intervals, Theil–Sen estimation, and Mann–Kendall testing to help distinguish long-term trends from year-to-year variability.

EarthScope also provides explanations tailored to students, the general public, and scientists, making environmental data easier to understand.

Our goal is to make NASA Earth science data more accessible, encourage climate awareness, and help communities explore how their environment is changing over time.
details:
The Problem

Understanding environmental change requires access to reliable data and meaningful statistical analysis. Although NASA makes extensive Earth science datasets publicly available, interpreting these records can be challenging for people without programming or scientific backgrounds.

Our Solution

EarthScope — Ocean Observatory is an interactive environmental data analysis platform that makes NASA Earth science data easier to explore and understand.

The application focuses primarily on the Caribbean while allowing users to analyze custom geographic coordinates anywhere in the world.

EarthScope addresses four essential questions: What is changing? Where is it changing? How much is it changing? Are these changes statistically significant?

How It Works

EarthScope retrieves historical monthly temperature and relative humidity data through NASA's POWER API, using model-derived meteorological information from MERRA-2.

The application validates and processes the records, calculates annual averages using complete years, and applies statistical methods to identify environmental trends.

These methods include linear regression, 95% confidence intervals, statistical significance testing, Theil–Sen slope estimation, and the Mann–Kendall test.

Users can visualize historical trends, compare two geographic locations, examine statistical results, and download processed datasets.

Accessibility and Creativity

EarthScope combines environmental data analysis with an accessible scientific dashboard called Ocean Observatory.

A key feature is its ability to explain results at three levels: Student, General Public, and Scientist. These explanations are generated from predefined templates using actual calculated values rather than AI-generated scientific conclusions.

Interactive charts, geographic context, downloadable CSV files, and transparent documentation make the application useful for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Intended Impact

EarthScope aims to make environmental trends easier to understand, particularly for Caribbean communities.

The platform can support environmental education, data literacy, research exploration, and public awareness of long-term environmental change.

Technologies Used

Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Plotly, Requests, GitHub and NASA POWER.

Scientific Transparency

EarthScope uses NASA model-derived estimates for individual geographic grid cells, not direct measurements from local weather stations or national averages.

The application identifies statistical uncertainty, documents its methodology, and explains that observed trends do not independently establish their causes.
